objectives.description: Create lint-agent-contracts.sh modeled on lint-contract-compliance.sh structure
objectives.note: Uses set -euo pipefail (matching lint-contract-compliance.sh exactly), color constants, --verbose/--help parsing, log_pass/log_fail/log_warn helpers, PASSED/FAILED/WARNINGS counters, lettered check functions, and the same summary/exit-code contract, as specified. Verified -e does not cause premature exit: all conditional greps are tested within if/&&/|| contexts, safe under set -e; re-ran both the clean pass and both negative fixtures after adding -e to confirm identical behavior. Root resolution deviates from the scripts/*.sh deploy-root-guard.sh convention: that guard is depth-specific to scripts/ (one level under .claude or .opencode) and, empirically verified, would misfire if sourced from scripts/lint/ (two levels deep) -- BASH_SOURCE[0] inside a sourced file resolves to the ORIGINAL calling script's path, not the guard's own path, so the guard's parent-directory check would see '.claude/scripts/lint' stripped to '.claude/scripts', never matching its '*/.claude' case pattern, and would reject even a validly-deployed invocation. Verified this empirically with a throwaway /tmp reproduction before deciding not to reuse the guard. Used git rev-parse --show-toplevel instead (safe for a read-only lint), falling back to REPO_ROOT env override, then a script-relative default -- this works identically whether invoked from the deployed .claude/scripts/lint/ copy or directly from the agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/lint/ source-store copy, which Phase 8's verification requires.

objectives.note: Verified in isolation: 78 total */agents/*.md glob matches, 75 dispatchable, excludes exactly core/agents/README.md and both lean/context/project/lean4/agents/lean-{research,implementation}-flow.md by name -- matches the plan's Scope Hypothesis exactly.

objectives.note: Verified against a scratch fixture: a rogue allowed-tools: key produces both a FAIL (invalid key) and a WARN (unknown key, since allowed-tools is also not in the supported set) -- both are correct, non-contradictory outcomes per the check's own stated behavior.

objectives.note: Verified against a scratch fixture: an agent with no model: field fails with the correct message.

objectives.description: Check C: no-task-references bullet presence, expected text read from the Phase 4 fragment file, fails loudly if fragment missing
objectives.note: In-scope set is a curated, path-relative allowlist (IN_SCOPE_RELATIVE_PATHS, 31 entries matching Phase 5's confirmed enumeration) since the classification rule ('authors deliverable files outside specs/**') is a judgment call not mechanically derivable from a file's own content -- documented inline in the script. Verified: temporarily renaming the fragment file produces the expected named FAIL ('canonical fragment not found ... cannot verify bullet text'); restored immediately after.
